title: Research Interests
text:
My academic interests are centered around the intersection of mathematics, machine learning, and signal processing.


I am interested in understanding the mathematical foundations of machine learning and how different learning approaches can be used to extract meaningful structure from data.



Signals and Systems introduced me to the mathematical representation and analysis of signals. This led to a growing interest in signal processing and its applications to real-world data.



I am particularly interested in image processing as a connection between signal processing, mathematics, and machine learning, especially in extracting meaningful information from complex visual data.



I am interested in the mathematical challenges that arise when working with high-dimensional data, including probabilistic methods and statistical learning.



Probability and statistics form an important part of my mathematical background and are areas I would like to explore further in the context of machine learning and data analysis.

title: Projects
text:
Here is a selection of academic and technical projects I have worked on through coursework and independent exploration.




A study of Tanaka’s Central Limit Theorem, focusing on its mathematical foundations and theoretical understanding.
Topics: Probability · Statistics · Mathematical Analysis







A machine learning project exploring anomaly detection in sequential data using One-Class SVM and Hidden Markov Models.
Topics: Machine Learning · Anomaly Detection · HMM · One-Class SVM







A study of two-dimensional Fourier transforms, Fresnel and Fraunhofer approximations, and diffraction through different apertures using theoretical analysis and Python simulations.
Topics: Signal Processing · Fourier Transform · Image Formation · Python







An embedded systems project involving ESP8266-based remote control, OTA firmware updates, configuration management, and network communication.
Topics: ESP8266 · IoT · Embedded Systems · OTA

title: Academic Background
text:
B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering
My undergraduate studies have provided me with a foundation in mathematics, probability, statistics, signal processing, and machine learning.




My mathematical preparation includes coursework and independent study in:

Linear Algebra
Probability
Statistics
High-Dimensional Probability
Mathematical Analysis

These subjects have shaped my interest in understanding the mathematical structure behind machine learning and data-driven problems.





Introduced me to fundamental machine learning concepts and probabilistic approaches to learning.



Provided a mathematical foundation for analyzing and representing signals and led to my interest in signal and image processing.



Developed my understanding of uncertainty, random variables, statistical inference, and probabilistic reasoning.



Provided essential mathematical tools for working with high-dimensional data and machine learning methods.




My interest in mathematics also developed through participation in the Iranian National Mathematics Olympiad, where I received a bronze medal.

title: Helia Tajabadi
text:
About
I am an Electrical Engineering student at Sharif University of Technology with a growing interest in mathematics, machine learning, and signal processing.
My interests have developed through coursework in probability, statistics, linear algebra, machine learning, and signals and systems. I am particularly interested in understanding the mathematical ideas behind learning from data and signal analysis, and I am currently exploring these areas through coursework and academic projects.
I enjoy working on problems that combine mathematical reasoning with computational methods, and I hope to further develop my research interests through academic research and collaboration.
